notes: The RTL has mutually exclusive FPGA and ASIC generate branches; the zero-register override can modify reg_file(0) only in the FPGA branch, while the ASIC branch fixes reg_file(0) to zero and generates writes only for indices 1 through the maximum address.

C4 lists only I under Objectives At Risk although its Phase 1 rubric marks Undermined Expected Behavior yes; the behavior is treated as an integrity consequence because the rubric reason says it makes later operand outputs incorrect.

points.reason: The generate branch stores register-file values, fixes register zero, and its stored values are later returned by the operand-read processes.
This process writes register-file entries from rd_i under the selected write condition, while the stored entries are read by the operand outputs.
This process writes reg_file from rd_i and returns selected stored words on rs1_o and rs2_o.

points.reason: opa_addr indexes the register written by rd_i, so corrupting the selection redirects the update.

points.reason: The control fields decide the indexed register-file entry that accepts rd_i in the ASIC branch.
The control fields determine whether opa_addr selects rf_rd or rf_rs1, changing which register value is returned on rs1_o.

points.reached by: the arrow register_file_fpga --> register_file (line 82) [opa_addr, rf_we] reaches the indexed reads
points.reason: opa_addr and ctrl_i.rf_rs2 index reg_file for the rs1_o and rs2_o assignments, so altered selections substitute different source operands.

points.reached by: the arrow rs3_enabled --> rs3_read [rs3_addr] reaches the indexed third read
points.reason: rs3_addr indexes reg_file for the rs3_o assignment.
The FPGA branch forms rf_we from the zero-register test and override, then selects address zero and writes it when the override is asserted, bypassing constant-zero behavior.

points.reached by: the arrow register_file_fpga --> register_file (line 82) [opa_addr, rf_we] reaches the protected write

points.reason: This branch only generates write processes for entries 1 through the maximum address and therefore does not provide a control path that writes register zero.
